additives.name: Tartrazine
additives.description: Bright lemon-yellow azo dye used in soft drinks, confectioneries, chips, and instant noodles to give an artificial vibrant color.
additives.fssai_status: Permitted with strict quantitative limits in specified food categories.

abroad_status.EU: Requires mandatory warning label: 'May have an adverse effect on activity and attention in children'
abroad_status.UK: Voluntary phase-out recommended following the Southampton Study

additives.health_considerations: Linked to hyperactivity and behavioral changes in sensitive children. Known to trigger allergic reactions, asthma, and urticaria in aspirin-intolerant individuals.

additives.name: Sunset Yellow FCF
additives.description: Petroleum-derived orange azo dye used to give foods an orange or apricot hue.
additives.fssai_status: Permitted with limits in specified processed foods.

abroad_status.EU: Requires warning: 'May have an adverse effect on activity and attention in children'

additives.health_considerations: Can induce hives, rhinitis, and hyperactivity in pediatric consumers.

additives.name: Carmoisine
additives.description: Synthetic red azo dye used in jams, jellies, and desserts.
additives.fssai_status: Permitted in specified foods with maximum limit of 100 mg/kg.

abroad_status.US: Not approved by the FDA for food use
abroad_status.EU: Requires mandatory child attention warning label

additives.health_considerations: Southampton dye associated with behavioral hyperactivity; can provoke intolerance in asthmatics.

additives.name: Ponceau 4R
additives.description: Strawberry red synthetic dye used in sweets, beverages, and dessert mixes.
additives.fssai_status: Permitted in specific food groups with limits.

abroad_status.US: Banned for food use by the FDA

additives.health_considerations: Allergenic potential and histamine liberator; banned in the United States.

additives.name: Erythrosine
additives.description: Cherry-pink synthetic dye commonly used in canned cherries, baked decorations, and candies.
additives.fssai_status: Permitted with strict restrictions.

abroad_status.US: Banned by the FDA in foods and ingested drugs in 2025 due to animal thyroid tumor studies
abroad_status.EU: Restricted exclusively to cocktail cherries and candied cherries

additives.health_considerations: Associated with thyroid hormone disruption and thyroid tumors in animal studies.

additives.name: Allura Red AC
additives.description: Dark red azo dye used widely in global confectionery, gelatin, and sodas.
additives.fssai_status: Not among India's 8 permitted coal-tar colours.

abroad_status.EU: Requires mandatory warning label regarding children's attention

additives.health_considerations: Associated with gut inflammation and mild behavioral changes in clinical pediatric trials.

additives.name: Caramel IV (Sulphite Ammonia)
additives.description: Dark brown coloring synthesized by heat treatment of carbohydrates with ammonium and sulfite compounds. Ubiquitous in colas, soy sauce, and gravies.
additives.fssai_status: Permitted in beverages and sauces.

abroad_status.US: California Proposition 65 listing for 4-MEI byproduct threshold

additives.health_considerations: Manufacturing process can produce trace levels of 4-Methylimidazole (4-MEI), a suspected animal carcinogen monitored by food safety authorities.

additives.name: Titanium Dioxide
additives.description: White mineral pigment used to make salad dressings, coffee creamers, chewing gum, and cake frostings look brightly opaque white.
additives.fssai_status: Currently permitted in chewing gum and specific confections under FSSAI standards.

abroad_status.EU: Banned as a food additive across the entire European Union since 2022 (EFSA concluded genotoxicity cannot be ruled out)

additives.health_considerations: Nanoparticles can accumulate in systemic organs; European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) determined it can no longer be considered safe due to potential DNA damage.

additives.name: Sorbic Acid
additives.description: Naturally derived or synthetic antimicrobial agent that inhibits mold and yeast growth.
additives.fssai_status: Permitted across dairy, cheese, baked goods.
additives.health_considerations: Generally well tolerated, metabolizes naturally like fatty acids.

additives.name: Potassium Sorbate
additives.description: Potassium salt of sorbic acid used to inhibit molds in cheese, dips, syrups, and packaged bread.
additives.fssai_status: Permitted within designated limits.
additives.health_considerations: Extensively studied and considered safe at regulatory levels; rare contact dermatitis in sensitive individuals.

additives.name: Sodium Benzoate
additives.description: A widely used chemical preservative that halts bacterial and fungal spoilage in acidic foods like fruit juices, carbonated soft drinks, pickles, and sauces.
additives.fssai_status: Permitted Class II preservative.
additives.health_considerations: When combined with Vitamin C (Ascorbic Acid, INS 300) in beverages under heat or light, it can react to form trace amounts of Benzene, a known carcinogen. May trigger allergies in asthmatics.

additives.name: Sulphur Dioxide
additives.description: Inorganic gas dissolved in dried fruits, wines, and fruit pulps to prevent enzymatic browning and bacterial decay.
additives.fssai_status: Permitted with mandatory allergen declaration.

abroad_status.EU: Mandatory allergen declaration when exceeding 10 mg/kg

additives.health_considerations: Known severe bronchospasm trigger in asthmatic individuals. Must be declared as a major allergen.

additives.name: Butylated Hydroxyanisole (BHA)
additives.description: Synthetic phenolic antioxidant used to prevent vegetable oils, potato chips, and butter from turning rancid.
additives.fssai_status: Permitted in fats and oils up to 200 mg/kg.

abroad_status.EU: Classified under review for endocrine disruption potential

additives.health_considerations: Listed as a reasonably anticipated human carcinogen by the US National Toxicology Program; exhibits mild endocrine-disrupting activity in animal models.

additives.name: Butylated Hydroxytoluene (BHT)
additives.description: Lipophilic organic compound added to packaging and oil-rich snacks to preserve freshness.
additives.fssai_status: Permitted in edible oils and fats with limits.
additives.health_considerations: Can accumulate in fatty tissues; suspected mild endocrine disruptor.

additives.name: Lecithin
additives.description: Natural phospholipid extracted from soybeans or sunflower seeds, essential for blending cocoa butter and solids in chocolate and bakery goods.
additives.fssai_status: Permitted without quantitative limit (GMP).
additives.health_considerations: Safe natural food component. Individuals with severe soy allergies must note source.

additives.name: Citric Acid
additives.description: Weak organic acid found naturally in citrus fruits, produced commercially via Aspergillus fermentation to impart a sour tang and preserve beverages.
additives.fssai_status: Permitted under Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP).
additives.health_considerations: Safe metabolic intermediate in the Krebs cycle. High chronic intake in acidic sodas can cause tooth enamel erosion.

additives.name: Carrageenan
additives.description: Polysaccharide extracted from red edible seaweeds, used to give body and creaminess to plant-based milks, ice creams, and processed meats.
additives.fssai_status: Permitted in dairy products and desserts.

abroad_status.EU: Permitted for general foods, but prohibited in infant formulas

additives.health_considerations: Numerous gastrointestinal studies suggest food-grade carrageenan may trigger gut inflammation, alter the microbiome, and worsen irritable bowel syndrome (IBS).

additives.name: Guar Gum
additives.description: Natural galactomannan polysaccharide extracted from guar beans (Cyamopsis tetragonoloba), common in sauces, dressings, and baked goods.
additives.fssai_status: Permitted GMP.
additives.health_considerations: Beneficial soluble dietary fiber; excessive consumption may cause mild bloating or gas.

additives.name: Xanthan Gum
additives.description: Polysaccharide fermented by Xanthomonas campestris, used widely in gluten-free baking and dressings for smooth texture.
additives.fssai_status: Permitted GMP.
additives.health_considerations: Safe natural stabilizer; fermented soluble fiber.

additives.name: Brominated Vegetable Oil (BVO)
additives.description: Vegetable oil bonded with elemental bromine, formerly used to keep citrus flavor oils in suspension in sodas.
additives.fssai_status: Not permitted in any food in India.
additives.health_considerations: Bromine bioaccumulates in adipose tissue and organ lipids; linked to thyroid and neurological toxicity.

additives.name: Sodium Carboxymethyl Cellulose
additives.description: Chemically modified cellulose used as a bulking agent and texture stabilizer in ice creams, pastries, and low-calorie diet foods.
additives.fssai_status: Permitted across multiple processed categories.

abroad_status.EU: Permitted with ongoing re-evaluation by EFSA

additives.health_considerations: Recent Nature and Cell Host & Microbe clinical studies show dietary emulsifiers like CMC can degrade the protective intestinal mucosal layer and promote colitis.

additives.name: Sodium Carbonates
additives.description: Classic leavening agent used in baked cookies, biscuits, and batters to release CO2 bubbles.
additives.fssai_status: Permitted GMP.
additives.health_considerations: Safe mineral leavener; contributes to dietary sodium.

additives.name: Monosodium Glutamate (MSG)
additives.description: Sodium salt of glutamic acid, an amino acid that triggers the savory 'umami' taste receptors on the tongue.
additives.fssai_status: Permitted in specific food categories under GMP. Not permitted in infant foods.
additives.health_considerations: Global scientific consensus (FSSAI, FDA, EFSA, WHO) has debunked the 'Chinese Restaurant Syndrome' myth. Highly sensitive individuals may experience transient headaches at very high bolus doses.

additives.name: Disodium Guanylate
additives.description: Nucleotide salt that works synergistically with MSG to amplify savory umami flavors in chips and instant noodles.
additives.fssai_status: Permitted with limits.
additives.health_considerations: Metabolizes to purines; individuals with gout or uric acid stones should moderate intake.

additives.name: Disodium Inosinate
additives.description: Purine nucleotide flavor enhancer, usually derived from tapioca or fish/meat, combined with glutamate to heighten savoriness.
additives.fssai_status: Permitted with limits.
additives.health_considerations: Safe for general population; strict vegetarians should verify sourcing if not marked with green dot.

additives.name: Potassium Bromate
additives.description: Oxidizing chemical formerly used by commercial bakeries to make bread rise higher and bleach flour white.
additives.fssai_status: Completely BANNED in India since 2016 following CSE study.

abroad_status.US: Permitted (FDA requires warning on flour bags)

additives.health_considerations: Classified by IARC as a Group 2B possible human carcinogen; nephrotoxic and thyroid toxin.

additives.name: Aspartame
additives.description: Low-calorie artificial sweetener roughly 200 times sweeter than sucrose, composed of aspartic acid and phenylalanine.
additives.fssai_status: Permitted with mandatory warning: 'Contains Phenylalanine - Not recommended for Phenylketonurics'.

abroad_status.WHO/IARC: Classified in 2023 as Group 2B (Possibly carcinogenic to humans), with JECFA reaffirming ADI of 40 mg/kg bw

additives.health_considerations: Contraindicated for individuals with phenylketonuria (PKU). Emerging research points to glucose intolerance and microbiome alterations with heavy chronic intake.

additives.name: Cyclamate
additives.description: Early synthetic non-caloric sweetener 30–50 times sweeter than table sugar.
additives.fssai_status: Removed from India's permitted additive list in 2016.

abroad_status.US: Banned by the FDA since 1970 due to bladder tumor concerns in rodents

additives.health_considerations: Banned in multiple major jurisdictions over carcinogenicity concerns.

additives.name: Sucralose
additives.description: Chlorinated carbohydrate approximately 600 times sweeter than sucrose, resistant to heat degradation in baking.
additives.fssai_status: Permitted with mandatory front-of-pack advisory for non-caloric sweetener.
additives.health_considerations: Passes mostly unabsorbed; clinical trials indicate potential reduction in beneficial gut Bifidobacteria and altered insulin sensitivity when paired with carbohydrates.

additives.name: Maltitol
additives.description: Hydrogenated maltose used in 'sugar-free' chocolates and protein bars. Imparts 75–90% of sugar's sweetness with half the calories.
additives.fssai_status: Permitted in sugar-free confectioneries with laxative effect advisory.

abroad_status.EU: Mandatory warning: 'Excessive consumption may produce laxative effects'

additives.health_considerations: High glycemic index among sugar alcohols (GI ~35–52 for syrup). Causes severe osmotic bloating, cramps, and diarrhea in sensitive guts.

additives.name: Plain Caramel (Caramel I)
additives.description: Natural or heat-synthesized brown food color produced by controlled heating of carbohydrates. Gives energy drinks, colas, and sauces their amber-brown color.
additives.fssai_status: Permitted GMP.
additives.health_considerations: Generally recognized as safe; lacks 4-MEI chemical compounds present in ammonia-treated caramel III/IV.

additives.name: Riboflavins
additives.description: Yellow-orange micronutrient (Vitamin B2) also used as a natural colorant in energy drinks and fortified cereals.
additives.fssai_status: Permitted GMP.
additives.health_considerations: Essential water-soluble B-vitamin; safe at normal dietary levels.
